summary: One small buy: SAM, $15, about 2.4% of equity. It goes into the Market Analyst's favored Staples sector, carries its own stop rather than the SPY 200-day line, and leaves cash near 11.4%, which is above the 10% buffer. I propose no adds to VOO or VTI and no sells, because no price stop or qualitative clause has tripped. Book review (L7): every stop block is 'ok' except VOO and VTI, which are NEAR. Those two make up about 23.5% of equity and share one stop: an SPY close below its 200-day (now 729.58 in market.json; the stored 729.31 is stale) trips both, and they should then be sold together next run. The qualitative clauses are all untripped. VOO/VTI: RSP 21d is +2.26%, which is positive. WMT: XLP 21d is +5.68%, above +3%. The WMT 11-16 8-K 5.02 matches a director appointment by inference, and the print is 11-19. KR: Stifel initiated at $80, and the cyber incident is still unconfirmed. INCY and EXEL: no new 8-K. EXEL sits only 3.2% above its $65 stop after Morgan Stanley's $57 target, so it is the closest to tripping. MCO and EXEL: both are still on the menu, which is now dated 11-17, so their 'screen drops it' clauses can trip but have not. VRSN: ex-dividend $0.81 today, a mechanical move. FAST: its stored 'marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging' condition is being met (XLI 21d -1.25%, 4.13% below its 200-day, and Industrials is on the avoid list). I am not selling it, because it is +6.5% on cost with beta 0.51 and no clause has tripped, but it is the first single stock to cut if cash is needed. For the PM's thesis_updates (L6): re-date the SPY 200-day to 729.58. Make MCO's text agree with its $470 stop (8% under $509.04 is $468.32). Add VTI's dollar level (8% under $375.22 is about $345.20). The exposure packet still files MCO under Industrials by bucket, not Financials, so the Financials weight is understated: MSCI+MCO together are about 8.3%. Lessons: I followed the Market Analyst's 'do not add to VOO/VTI ahead of the Nvidia print' over the owner's invested-goal default (L4/L9), and sized SAM for the Staples overlap with WMT and KR (L3).

proposals.thesis: Consumer Staples is one of the Market Analyst's three favored sectors today (XLP 5d +1.88%, 21d +5.68%, 10.06% above its 200-day), and he asks to keep new risk small and in those sectors. SAM is rank 7 in the Fundamentals Analyst's list: F8 (only current_ratio_improved fails), gp_sector_pct 0.945, CFO $270M about 2.5x net income $108M, no flags and a current fiscal year. Its 252-day beta is -0.27 (+$2.72 per $100 in the 10% stress test, per the packet), so it does not add to the SPY 200-day stop that VOO and VTI share (L9). Dates (L2): the News Analyst puts the next earnings at 2027-02-23, outside the window, and lists the 11-13 8-K 8.01 as still unread with no headline. Its content is unverified, and I say so rather than calling it routine. Overlap (L3): by bucket, Staples is already 13.9% (WMT 8.05%, KR 5.85%), and WMT and KR have moved together on down days. This adds about 2.4%, taking the bucket to about 16.3% two sessions before WMT's 11-19 print, which is why the size is $15 against a $65.77 cap. SAM is a brewer, not a grocer, so it is a different business inside the same factor. L4: the buy rests on the favored-sector call and the name's own quality, not on diversification alone. Net income is thin against $1.96B of revenue, so the Fundamentals Analyst's concern stands. The fundamentals data predates the Q3 print.
proposals.invalidation: SAM closes at or below $205.00, which is about 8.2% under the $223.29 menu close; the stop is to be restated from the actual fill at the next run (L6). Also invalid if the 11-13 8-K 8.01 or a later 8-K turns out to report a guidance cut, or if the fundamentals screen drops SAM from the menu.
